prompt: Assess this claim: Indigenous people are overrepresented in prison populations.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is **well supported in several countries, but needs a geographic qualifier**.

“Overrepresented” means Indigenous people make up a larger share of the prison population than of the general population. This pattern is documented in countries including Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, where Māori are Indigenous. Its extent varies by jurisdiction, year, and whether the figures include remand, sentenced prisoners, or youth detention.

The disparity alone does not establish its causes. Relevant factors include historical dispossession, socioeconomic disadvantage, policing practices, access to legal representation, and sentencing decisions. It does not demonstrate an inherent propensity toward crime.

A more precise claim is: **“Indigenous people are overrepresented in prison populations in many jurisdictions, including Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.”**
